title: Show HN: Parseable, an open observability datalake, handles 100M time-series/min
summary: Parseable is an open-source observability datalake platform designed for high-volume log, metric, and trace ingestion. It claims to handle 100 million time-series data points per minute, positioning itself as a scalable, cost-effective alternative to commercial observability solutions.
problem_solved: Provides a scalable, open-source solution for managing massive-scale observability data at a fraction of the cost of commercial platforms like Datadog or Splunk.
why_valuable: Enables organizations to handle extreme data volumes (100M+ time-series/min) with an open, vendor-neutral observability stack that integrates with existing S3-compatible storage infrastructure.
